Change c0260. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. XIV.

Context before (unchanged): The injustice of his sentence was very flagrant; all Paris was indignant; and it was judged that his religion and wealth, rather than the crime alleged against him, had been the cause of his condemnation.

1818 text: "Felix had been present at the trial; his horror and indignation were uncontrollable, when he heard the decision of the court.

1831 text: "Felix had accidentally been present at the trial; his horror and indignation were uncontrollable, when he heard the decision of the court.

Diff: " Felix had {+accidentally+} been present at the trial; his horror and indignation were uncontrollable, when he heard the decision of the court.

Context after (unchanged): He made, at that moment, a solemn vow to deliver him, and then looked around for the means.

result.rationale: Insertion of "accidentally" before "been present at the trial" adds an adverb qualifying Felix's presence; it alters how his attendance is framed but not the events, so it is a stylistic qualification with slight characterization effect.
